summary: A 1905 wooden fire lookout from Squaw Mountain, replaced by steel in 1919, moved after 2011 and now standing beside the Moosehead Lake Region Visitor Center in Greenville.

facts.design: Steel tower with a wooden cab; Maine Geographic reports a replica of the fire warden's cabin has been added

access.note: Beside the Moosehead Lake Region Visitor Center on Route 15 in Greenville; a Maine Geographic article calls it worth a visit. Climbing is not addressed.

events.note: First tower, a 22-foot wood and log structure erected by the M.G. Shaw Lumber Company; put into operation June 10, 1905
Steel tower replaced the wooden one; the register's Built field, WMTW and Maine Geographic all give 1919
Register description says the present steel tower with wooden cab was built in 1959; no other source gives this date
Maine Memory says the tower was closed for good and replaced by aircraft patrols; WMTW says watchmen staffed it until 1976
WMTW: the fire watchmen maintained a constant presence until 1976
Register entry US 67, ME 3 for the Squaw Mountain site, registered August 7, 1993
Removed from the summit; WMTW says the cab was removed by helicopter; Maine Geographic says the tower was removed
Maine Memory: relocated in October 2012 to the Natural Resource Education Center in Greenville
Maine Geographic: reassembled in 2015 adjacent to the Moosehead Lake Region Visitor Center on Route 15

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1905 is the first wooden tower and 1919 is its steel replacement, per WMTW and Maine Geographic; the register's 1959 date for the present steel tower is not supported by other sources and is left unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on several dates and on what was moved. Staffing end: WMTW says 1976, Maine Memory says the tower closed in 1968. Move: WMTW says the cab went to the visitor center in 2011 by helicopter; Maine Geographic says the tower was reassembled in 2015; Maine Memory says October 2012 to the Natural Resource Education Center. The register's 1959 date for the present steel tower conflicts with 1919 elsewhere. The register entry (US 67) still describes the summit site, not Greenville. Agency for the Greenville tower is not documented (the register lists the Maine Dept. of Conservation for the summit site), so it is left out. The NREC page (nrecmoosehead.org) returned 404 and was not used. Access is marked public only because the tower sits beside a visitor center that Maine Geographic calls worth a visit; climbing is not documented. The Commons photo already in the record was not re-added. Page reads: about 6 distinct pages, plus one search.
